title: Shakshuka
subtitle: Eggs poached in a spiced tomato and pepper sauce
excerpt: The North African and Israeli brunch classic: eggs poached directly in a thick, aromatic sauce of tomatoes, red peppers, onion, cumin, and smoked paprika until the whites are just set and the yolks remain runny. Eaten from the pan with flatbread.

recipe.sourceNotes: Shakshuka (the name is thought to derive from an Arabic or Berber word meaning mixture or all mixed up) is a dish of eggs poached in a spiced tomato sauce that is eaten across North Africa, the Middle East, and the Levant. It is particularly associated with Israeli breakfast culture, where it arrived through the large communities of Libyan and Tunisian Jewish immigrants in the twentieth century. The Israeli food writer and cook Yotam Ottolenghi brought the dish to wide British attention in the 2000s and 2010s. The sauce recipe varies considerably: harissa is sometimes added for heat; preserved lemon for acidity; crumbled feta stirred in at the end for richness. The essential form is eggs cooked in a spiced tomato sauce; everything else is variation.

recipeTools.notes: A wide frying pan or sauté pan with a lid.

content.text: Make wells in the sauce before adding the eggs: the sauce should be thick enough to hold the eggs in place. Cover the pan for the final cooking so the steam sets the top of the whites without the yolks overcooking. Watch carefully: the difference between perfectly runny yolks and hard ones is about 2 minutes. Remove the pan from the heat while the whites are just barely set; they will continue cooking in the residual heat.

Heat the olive oil in a wide frying pan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 8 minutes until soft and golden. Add the red peppers and cook for 5 minutes. Add the garlic, cumin, smoked paprika, cayenne, and harissa (if using) and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tinned tomatoes and simmer for 10 minutes until the sauce is thick and rich. Season with salt. Taste: it should be deeply savoury with a clear spice backbone.

Make 6 wells in the sauce with the back of a spoon. Crack one egg into each well. Cover the pan and cook over low heat for 6 to 8 minutes until the whites are just set and the yolks are still runny. Remove from the heat. Scatter with parsley and crumbled feta. Serve immediately from the pan with flatbread or crusty bread.
